prize_parts.citation: for developing targeted protein degradation by chemically induced proximity, through heterobifunctional PROTAC degraders and the identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide-type molecular glue degraders

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B019 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The case rests on one design principle that both strands share, recruiting an E3 ubiquitin ligase to a chosen protein so that the target is removed rather than inhibited. That principle changed what chemists and clinicians can do. It makes proteins without a conventional binding pocket tractable, and it gives biologists a way to deplete a protein acutely. It has been reproduced by many independent laboratories and supported by ternary-complex structures. Crews and Deshaies supplied the concept and first demonstrations of PROTACs. Handa identified cereblon as the target of thalidomide, which is the mechanistic basis of the molecular-glue degraders and links the glue strand to the PROTAC strand through the same E3-ligase hijacking logic. A citation written around the principle rather than a single approved product is also what I think the committee can defend in one sentence.
statement.case_against: The credit is crowded and a three-name cap forces a cut that will look arbitrary to some: Ciulli (VHL ligands, structure-guided design), Sakamoto (first PROTAC with Crews and Deshaies), Gray, Ito and Kim are all left out. Round 1 showed that Aqvist, Somfai and Brzezinski regard PROTACs and cereblon glues as two partly distinct discoveries, so my unified citation is the most contestable part of the proposal. Clinical validation is also incomplete: from memory, no degrader is approved, and nothing in the files settles this. If the committee requires a delivered medicine and durable efficacy, recognition could be a year or two early. I also remain uneasy that my trio is not the only one that fits, since four members share it and one prefers Ciulli.

responses.point: Aqvist keeps Ciulli as the third name for a PROTAC-only citation, argues that Handa's work explains a drug already in clinical use, and says the glue arm would make the prize harder to state in one sentence.
responses.response: I have reconsidered this seriously and I still land on Handa. I agree that Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures are what made PROTAC design rational, and a PROTAC-only prize with Ciulli would be coherent. But the citation then has to omit the mechanism by which thalidomide-type drugs, the best-established clinical degrader class, actually work. Handa's cereblon identification is not only an explanation of an old drug. It is the discovery that showed a small molecule can reprogram an E3 ligase to a new substrate, which is the same principle Crews and Deshaies exploited with a bifunctional design. I therefore read the two as one principle seen from two sides, not as competing credit streams. I accept your point that the sentence is harder to write, and I have rewritten my citation to name the two mechanisms explicitly. If the committee insists on a PROTAC-only citation I could accept Ciulli, but I regard that as the narrower and less complete prize.

responses.point: Somfai says the PROTAC and cereblon glue stories should not be merged under one citation without a clear reason, and that a PROTAC-only citation will draw the Handa objection anyway.
responses.response: This is the right test and I would state my reason. The reason is that the shared claim is mechanistic, not historical: in both cases a small molecule brings a ligase and a neo-substrate into one ternary complex and the substrate is ubiquitinated and destroyed. The histories differ, since the thalidomide story began as a clinical observation and PROTACs as a design idea, but the molecular principle is the same, and cereblon is the ligase that links them because the most clinically advanced PROTACs also recruit it. You note, as I do, that a PROTAC-only citation is fragile on Handa. That is why I would rather accept a unified citation that is slightly broader than one that is easy to attack. On maturity, I accept that the clinical evidence is still being collected, but I do not think a chemistry prize for a principle needs an approval, and the independent replication you value in B034 is equally present here.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, still asks what Ciulli's work adds and whether approval status should be settled before the final ballots, and he keeps nanopore sequencing as a mature alternative with a cleaner physical principle.
responses.response: On the chair's request, what Ciulli adds is the structure-guided rational design of VHL-recruiting degraders and the quantitative ternary-complex cooperativity picture. That is real and important, but it refines the PROTAC strand rather than defining the principle, and I would credit it as such. On approval, I cannot verify it from the files and I do not think we should pretend otherwise. What I can say is that a prize does not need it, because the discovery is the principle and the evidence that it holds is structural and replicated. On nanopores, I respect the maturity and the clean physical principle, but I cannot see a trio that avoids omitting Bayley, Kasianowicz, Deamer, Branton or Akeson, and I share Somfai's and Zou's question whether the decisive step is chemistry. B019 has a stable three-name core. I would keep it ahead of B002 for that reason.

responses.point: Sparr says B045 is more mature than B019 if the committee wants a clinical approval, that she would favour Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli over adding glue names, and that she would prefer to see the PROTAC versus cereblon question settle.
responses.response: I agree that B045 is more mature clinically and I have kept it as an alternative for that reason. The pKa-tuned phase behaviour you describe is a real physical-chemical principle. My difficulty is still the seat count: Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer cannot be cut cleanly, and the overlap with Medicine 2023 makes it harder to justify as a separate Chemistry achievement. You ask for the PROTAC-cereblon question to be settled rather than forced into one citation. I would answer that the question is settled by the mechanism, not by history, and that the committee can now decide between the unified and the PROTAC-only citation without losing the underlying prize, since the round-1 statements that touch B019 accept the same underlying principle. If you can name a clean trio for B045 and a single discovery for its citation, I would reconsider it, but I do not think the discussion has produced that.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranked B019 seventh, asked for expert reports on whether the PROTAC and glue contributions can be separated, and said that choosing Ciulli over Handa should be debated explicitly rather than decided by default.
responses.response: I welcome the explicit debate and I think it has now happened in round 1, with Zou, Chabes, Linke and I choosing Handa and Aqvist choosing Ciulli with reasons. On your concern that eight names across two discoveries cannot be honestly compressed into three, I agree that a three-name cap does not do justice to Sakamoto, Gray, Ito, Kim or Ciulli. It is a limit of the prize, not of the science. Where we differ is whether that limit makes the field unsuitable. I do not think so: the principle is unified at the molecular level and the three-name core of Crews, Deshaies and Handa maps onto the concept, the first demonstration and the cereblon mechanism. I accept that your preference for the clean two-name attribution of B055 is a legitimate way to weigh the same evidence, though I share Aqvist's and Chabes's concern that it follows Marcus 1992 closely and reaches a narrower audience.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a unified PROTAC and cereblon citation, or require a PROTAC-only citation with Ciulli as the third name.
Clinical approval status of degraders, which I know only from memory and which the files do not settle.
Whether the third name Handa is sufficiently independent of the Ito and Sakamoto contributions on cereblon and the early thalidomide work.
Whether prior recognition in adjacent areas (Medicine 2023, Chemistry 2020) should lower the appetite for B043 or B045 as fallbacks.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict has arisen since round 1. I have no known collaboration or institutional tie to Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli or any other credited name on the shortlist. My earlier note about a self-assembly link to Emma Sparr remains a scientific interest and does not bear on B019. Several colleagues' disclosures in round 1 (Lund colleagues, Brzezinski's closeness to B055, Zou's closeness to B005 and B006, Sparr's closeness to B045) do not involve me.
